stem: A 35-year-old man has had a vasectomy reversed and has been unable to father a child for 18 months. His testosterone, FSH and LH are normal and there is no varicocele. Semen analysis shows sperm that clump together tail to tail and move poorly, though the count is adequate.
oneliner: 35M + vasectomy reversal + infertile 18 months + normal hormones, no varicocele + sperm clumped and poorly motile → what immune consequence?
ask: Which process best explains his infertility?

options.B: Leydig cell failure with low testosterone

whyNot.A: A **tumor** would not make sperm **clump tail to tail**
whyNot.B: **Low testosterone** is excluded by his **normal hormones**
whyNot.D: **Retrograde ejaculation** gives low volume and sperm in post-void urine, not clumping

why: Vasectomy lets sperm leak from the blocked duct, exposing **sperm antigens** normally hidden behind the **blood-testis barrier**. The body makes **antisperm antibodies** that **agglutinate** sperm and impair motility, so he is **infertile** despite normal hormones.
chain: Vasectomy: sperm leak from the blocked duct
Haploid sperm antigens meet the immune system

idea.rule: Breaking a hidden-antigen barrier turns self into foreign.
also: Mumps orchitis and testicular trauma can do the same
Spermatic granuloma follows sperm leakage after vasectomy
Mixed antiglobulin reaction test detects antisperm antibodies
